title: fix: live updates defer indefinitely during active conversations
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS live updater indefinitely defers an update when a Gateway conversation remains active.

## User Impact

Updates can finish through a bounded, recovery-preserving interruption. Pending lifecycle writes still prevent the Gateway from stopping; older idle-only residents continue to defer safely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing maintenance-drain owner with the installation's trusted built control client and validated LaunchAgent binding. It closes admission, verifies write custody, and commits shutdown against the serving process before native bootout. The adapter revalidates the maintenance lock, checkout, service environment, and resident identity.

## Evidence

- New updater boundary cases failed against the previous helper and pass with this change: ordinary active work reaches committed shutdown before build; held write custody refuses stop/build and resumes the lease. Resident protocol fixtures match the inspected prior source contract; they do not execute a published package.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/openclaw-live-updater.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 53 passed, 1 platform skip; 38.74 seconds wall. New cases take about 3.4 seconds total, adding approximately 3.4 CI seconds on macOS.
- `pnpm test src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-drain.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-drain.native.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 59 passed, 14 environment/platform skips; 26.05 seconds wall.
- Root scripts type graph, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Fresh autoreview completed. Its sole finding assumed bare Node source resolution; rejected with direct runtime evidence: the documented `node --import tsx` invocation successfully loads all three production owner modules, reporting their exported operations as functions. The existing standalone fixture runner also explicitly installs the loader. No plain-Node support is claimed.
